description: Arab kingdom of the Banu Lakhm, ruling from the city of al-Hira on the lower Euphrates as a client of the Sasanian Persian empire. The Lakhmids fielded auxiliary cavalry on the Persian side of the long Roman-Persian wars and competed with the Byzantine-aligned Ghassanids across the Syrian Desert. Their deposition by Khusrau II in 602 deprived the Sasanians of an Arab buffer state and is sometimes cited as a contributing factor to the early Islamic conquest of Mesopotamia a generation later.

temporal.notes: Arab client kingdom of the Sasanian Persians centred on al-Hira on the lower Euphrates; deposed by the Sasanian king Khusrau II in 602, after which the Sasanians administered the frontier directly.

geographic.notes: Capital al-Hira on the lower Euphrates south of Kufa; the polity controlled tribal-bedouin frontiers between Sasanian Mesopotamia and inland Arabia.
